brand.essence: Senior CFO leadership that builds the finance function a scale-up needs: compliant, in control and optimised for growth.
brand.positioning: ScaleUp Financial Management is the senior finance partner that takes a growing company from informal bookkeeping to a professional finance function, one stage at a time: op orde, in control, meer inzicht, beter schaalbaar. Diagnosis, roadmap, hands-on implementation and ongoing operation, led by Wilgert Hart with nearly 30 years of senior finance leadership and backed by a network of finance professionals.
brand.audience: Owners and boards of NL-based start-ups making the scale-up transition (€1M–€20M revenue, growing fast, finance still informal).
brand.toneOfVoice: Plain Dutch. No jargon, no false urgency. Speaks like a senior CFO at a board table: direct, honest about what's broken, confident about how to fix it.

stages.promise_nl: Een administratie die klopt en aan de regels voldoet: boekhouding, btw, loonadministratie en jaarwerk op tijd en zonder verrassingen.
stages.promise_en: Books that are right and compliant: bookkeeping, VAT, payroll and year-end on time and without surprises.
stages.bridges: small: canal bridges, wooden drawbridges, Magere Brug

stages.promise_nl: Een vaste maandafsluiting en rapportages waar je op kunt sturen.
stages.promise_en: A fixed month-end close and reporting you can steer on.

stages.promise_nl: Prognoses, kasstroom en KPI's die vooruitkijken in plaats van terug.
stages.promise_en: Forecasts, cash flow and KPIs that look ahead instead of back.

stages.promise_nl: Een financiële functie die is ingericht op groei: marges en werkkapitaal geoptimaliseerd, klaar voor investeerders, banken en overnames.
stages.promise_en: A finance function built for growth: margins and working capital optimised, ready for investors, banks and acquisitions.

principles: Amber is a signal, not decoration — one amber element per surface (logo cap, CTA button, or data accent), never both a button and a link amber on the same page.
Body text is navy, not black — warmth and authority together; pure black reads cold and impersonal for a finance partner.
Backgrounds default to warm Paper (#FAF8F3), not pure white — paper reads as a professional partner, white reads as a software product.
The Step Rail motif is a signature, not a pattern — used once per visible surface, never tiled at full opacity outside the background pattern tile (≤8% opacity).
Board-table voice: name what is broken, then say what fixes it. No jargon, no false urgency, no brochure register.

One name, one tagline, one headline: the ScaleUp wordmark, 'Start to Scale' as the sign-off in NL and EN, and the NL staircase ('Van risico naar regie. Van intuïtie naar inzicht. Van start-up naar serieuze scale-up.') as the hero headline on covers and the home page.
The four bars are four stages (Op orde, In control, Meer inzicht, Beter schaalbaar). Services, site sections, deck chapters and the bridge imagery are ordered on that ladder, small to big.

treatments.note: Named house looks applied DOWNSTREAM (format-MCP render + website CSS), never pre-baked into the library. Navy Duotone is the house look for the bridge library (operator pick D2, 2026-10-14; Warme schemer was the alternative on the client board): heroes, covers, dividers. Daylight for the rare natural-colour moment; amber-graded for one warm section at most; paper-mono for textures only. The navy scrim (images.overlay) is a separate text-safety layer.

daylight.label: Daylight
daylight.usage: Natural colour, slightly muted, warm paper lift in the highlights. Calm and factual; for the rare natural-colour moment (Navy Duotone is the house look).

paper-mono.label: Paper Mono
paper-mono.usage: Black-and-white with fine grain, for background textures (deck planks, steps, railings) only, never the house look for whole bridges.

navy-duotone.label: Navy Duotone
navy-duotone.usage: Signature deep-navy wash for covers + hero moments — navy shadows through slate mids to warm-paper highlights, applied transparently so the photo breathes. The structured-authority signature.

amber-graded.label: Amber Graded
amber-graded.usage: Restrained cinematic grade for section imagery — mostly neutral, a whisper of Signal Amber in the shadows and warm paper in the highlights. Kept subtle — the single amber accent per surface.

signatureElements: Step Rail — four bars in a fixed +18% geometric ascent (relative heights ≈ 0.40 / 0.59 / 0.79 / 1.00, bar width 16, gap 6, 1px radius), single-colour (amber on navy, navy on paper); the ascent itself is the signature — no two-tone cap.
Warm Paper background (#FAF8F3) as default surface, not pure white — distinguishes the advisory register from a software product.
Navy-90 / amber-10 horizontal divider (thin 1.5px line with amber terminal at right) — encodes the 'ascend' direction, structural punctuation between sections.
NL three-line tagline staircase as typographic hero — structurally echoes the Step Rail ascent and is never translated literally to English.
Archivo Bold (700, or 800 for display) with -0.02em tracking for all display and heading — an engineered grotesque that carries the Sage register as diagnostic clarity rather than literary warmth.

Archivo Semibold (600) overline caps at 0.20em tracking, 11px — labels sections, wordmark caption 'FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT', badges; hierarchy comes from weight + case + tracking within one family, not a second typeface.
JetBrains Mono reserved exclusively for numbers, tables, and data-adjacent contexts — signals that figures are decision-grade, not decoration.

Dutch bridges from small to big, one register per stage: canal and drawbridges for Op orde up to the iconic spans for Beter schaalbaar. Calm daylight or blue hour, never dramatic high-contrast black and white.
The stage ladder: four numbered steps that reuse the Step Rail proportions, used for services, process and deck chapters.
antiPatterns: Multiple amber elements on a single surface (amber is a single-use signal per page).
Pure black (#000000) or pure white (#FFFFFF) as primary background or body text — both break the warm advisory register.
Gradients on body sections (gradientDirection is 'none' by design; gradient only appears in nav-amber-diag pptx asset).
Tilted, rotated, or two-tone Step Rail motif — must be upright, single-colour bars (amber on navy, navy on paper), no exceptions.
Dropping a bar or adding a fifth — four bars in a +18% ascent is load-bearing meaning.
Mountains, Alpine or Dolomite scenery, or generic Dutch landscape (polders, tulips, windmills); bridges are the one landscape subject.
Handshake or suits-in-meeting stock photography — contra the architectural and data-clarity direction.
Mixed NL+EN within the same sentence in copy.
Buzzwords: 'synergy', 'next-level', 'agile', or any phrase that sounds like a brochure.
Pattern tile at full opacity on reading surfaces — restricted to 6–8% opacity on slide/section backgrounds only.
Bridges outside the Netherlands, or any photograph already used in another client's library.
Dramatic high-contrast black-and-white bridge photography as the house style.
A two-tone wordmark (Scale in one colour, Up in another).
requiredMotifs: Step Rail (four ascending bars) on all deliverable covers (small, left-aligned over section title in decks; as hero accent below the NL tagline on web).
Navy-90 / amber-10 thin-line divider as section rule on web and documents.
Warm Paper (#FAF8F3) as the default background surface on all light-mode deliverables.
White wordmark variant on all navy or image-overlay surfaces.
55% navy tint overlay on all hero and cover photograph treatments.
